**Causality** — causation and the structure of causal relations — causal order, definite and indefinite, and its combinatorics, topology and geometry; sheaf- and process-theoretic accounts of causality; causal models, causal inference and interventionist accounts of what a causal relation is; and the metaphysics of causation — exclusion, mental causation, causal emergence and closure, reciprocal causation (ADR-035).

| [CASE-337](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-337.md) | Beta–Bernoulli features vs shared-driver null | [LEAD-144](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-144.md)'s study, the "Option A" [CASE-165](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-165.md) recommends, in one linear family. Twenty-four members in six overlapping working groups, with a communication graph built from the groups, are simulated in three worlds: coupled along the graph; driven by one persistent external driver per group with no interaction; and half of each. The driver's gain is tuned so that every world shows the same within-group correlation, 0.30. CASE-165's finite beta-Bernoulli model (K = 16, α = 3) and four comparators are fitted to 600 days of each world and scored on interventions none was fitted to: a pulse to a member, and the cut of a group's internal ties. Over seven organizations, the feature model finds more features under the null (11.1) than under coupling (8.7), better aligned with the groups (Jaccard 0.72 against 0.44); read as causes of members it is exact under the driver and misses every cut under coupling, and read as realized by its holders it is wrong in both. The communication graph alone is right under coupling and invents coupling under the driver (a predicted cut effect of −0.18 where the truth is 0); the features added to it leave that error (0.21), and observing the true driver removes it (0.006). One-step fit ranks the models the same way in every world. The design, code and wording are the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-347](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-347.md) | Priced lagged block test on three populations | [LEAD-026](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-026.md) asked for [CASE-101](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-101.md)'s three populations to be run through [QUESTION-115](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md)'s search and a lagged block criterion ([QUESTION-116](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-116.md)). Four populations of six member slots with the same turnover were simulated, matched in member variance, member correlation and the aggregate's lag-1 autocorrelation: common input (A), norms transmitted at a lag of eight steps (B), an institution that trains, selects and answers to its members (C), and the same institution deaf to them (C0). A block test priced by [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)'s rule, over all subsets and windows of 1 to 16 steps, finds B's members alone, with the strongest support at the transmission lag. It joins A's members to their driver and C's and C0's to their institution, the same verdict for all three. C differs only by a feedback the price removes beyond four steps, and A and C0 get the same verdict on every measure. With the external variable unobserved, every arm's members pass. Retention conditioned on the environment survives turnover only in B; Bourrat's interventional retention of B's members does not, since intervening on the present misses the stored norms. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-354](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-354.md) | Walls in Z2-symmetric lattices | [LEAD-040](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-040.md) asked for A15's Experiment B: a family of small recurrent networks with a Z2 symmetry, trained on a task whose answer depends on boundaries in the input, with the four candidate partitions of the hidden field of [QUESTION-491](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-491.md) compared and walls moved by intervention. Six one-dimensional lattice networks (32 sites, 4 or 8 units per site, no bias, so the update is Z2-equivariant) were trained to report m², m the mean sign of a noisy domain input, held for 12 steps after the input was removed; four frozen random networks with trained readouts were the control. Five of the six learned static ordered phases with walls pinned to the lattice; one learned an oscillating phase. In the five, walls lay inside the causal-state coherent structures at every slice, and once the input was off flipping a wall site moved the answer (95 to 100% of wall sites) and moving a wall by interchange moved the answer as a wall model predicts (IIA 0.92 to 0.96, against 0.10 to 0.21 in the controls). Local transfer entropy was near zero at the pinned walls and marked under 3% of sites. While the input was on, the same interchange failed (IIA 0.03 to 0.32): the input put the wall back. A closed pair of walls did not shrink unless shorter than the training minimum; a wall forced by opposite boundary inputs, erased by writing a uniform state, reappeared at the clamped end in four of six networks and not at all in two. The design choices and wording are the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CASE-391](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-391.md) | Thermodynamics of prediction reproduced | [LEAD-005](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-005.md)'s first milestone for [QUESTION-494](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-494.md): reproduce a known no-feedback result, then add feedback. The result is Still, Sivak, Bell and Crooks (2012), already read ([LIT-327](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-327.md), [NOTE-295](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-295.md)) and held as [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md). In numpy (scratch/studies/lead-005/, 15 tests), 300 random 4-state systems driven by a 3-symbol Markov signal through Metropolis kernels satisfy the per-switch identity (Eq. 14), the summed identity (Eq. 17) and the heat identity (Eq. 19) to 3e-15, and the bounds (Eqs. 16, 18, 21) in every instance; no step's nostalgia is negative; Monte Carlo trajectories agree with the exact averages. With the drive made to depend on the system's state (500 systems), the identities and the summed bound still hold, but a step's nostalgia is negative in 405, the summed nostalgia in 323, and the dissipation and the excess work in 6. In an 8-percept loop where the predictive partition is a sticky nuisance and the interventional partition is the context the action must match, the memory that keeps only the context is the cheapest that does the task by every cost measured; the policy that uses it changes its nostalgia from ln 2 to 0 and leaves its heat per step unchanged. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
